notes: §1989:A.2.22.3 AR1: "Argument-1 must be class alphabetic or alphanumeric and must be at least one character in length." CheckArgumentClasses screens the Verified LOWER-CASE row at every edition: Violation admits class alphabetic, alphanumeric or national and PredicateViolation's minimum-width arm refuses a zero-length argument; the class national that 2023 adds cannot reach the screen at 85, where national items and literals are refused by UsageConstructId and VisitNonNumericLiteral (COBOL0900). Probed at 85: alphanumeric, alphabetic, group and edited items and a literal are accepted; a numeric item, a numeric literal, an arithmetic expression and an integer function are refused with COBOL1627. The witness is the numeric-item refusal.

next.reason: 1985: "Argument-1 must be class alphabetic or alphanumeric"; 2023: "Argument-1 shall be of class alphabetic, alphanumeric, or national". 2023 LOWER-CASE also accepts a class national argument-1, which 1985 refused; the one-character minimum length is unchanged.
